What it is (ADP meaning): ADP company code - which payroll company the batch posts to
How it is derived: Constant. companysetup is a single-row table joined with CROSS JOIN (ON 1=1)
Notes / gotchas: Always 'new01'. Same value also sits unused on dev_aloha.dbo.gblstore.ADPCompanyCode

What it is (ADP meaning): ADP paydata batch number - groups the rows into one batch per restaurant
Notes / gotchas: nvarchar, not int. For the 28 company stores it equals the store number. 6 franchise stores have '0' (no Batch ID configured) - they only appear if you run for all stores

What it is (ADP meaning): The employee's ADP file number (payroll ID)
How it is derived: Employee lookup: hstShift.Employee = employees.GUID AND hstShift.Store = employees.StoreGUID
Notes / gotchas: Set by HR inside Toast. Blank when unset - the row still exports but cannot post in ADP. This is also the only employee identifier in the file (no name column)

What it is (ADP meaning): Free-text label for the ADP batch
How it is derived: Same store lookup as Batch ID
Notes / gotchas: Cosmetic. Populated for only 41 of 95 stores and inconsistent ('Flowood', 'GPORT', 'NEW01', 'Corporate')

What it is (ADP meaning): Regular (non-overtime) hours worked in the pay period
How it is derived: SUM over the employee's shifts at that job code and rate

What it is (ADP meaning): Overtime hours worked in the pay period
How it is derived: SUM over the same grain as Reg Hours
Notes / gotchas: Column really is spelled OvertimeHOurs in SQL (capital O in Hours)

What it is (ADP meaning): ADP earnings code the tip dollars post under
Notes / gotchas: Same value is configured at contacts.dbo.companysetup.ADPTippedEarningsCode, but the proc does not read it

How it is derived: (RegHours + OTHours) * store TipsPerHour, rounded to 2dp per shift-group then summed. TipsPerHour = store non-cash tips / store non-salary hours for the period
Notes / gotchas: NOT the employee's own tips. It is a pooled redistribution: every non-salary employee at the store (dish, prep, expo included) earns the same dollars-per-hour. hstShift.NonCashTips exists but is ignored by this report

What it is (ADP meaning): ADP temporary-department override - which job the hours were worked in
Notes / gotchas: Rows where ExportID = 'NOREPORT' are dropped from the export. Blank-ExportID map rows (ToastJC 0 = Admin/Accounting) never surface because those job codes are SALARY
A mid-period raise produces two rows for the same employee and job code, one per rate
